title: unified-rollouts: probing staged shadow + canary + A/B autorollback workflows
author: Maya Chen
commit_list: a1f3d9c: add probing stage state machine and scheduler
c3d5f1b: wire probing traces into tracing and add hooks for shadow traffic sampling
d4e6a2c: add e2e test harness and fixtures for staged probing
description:
Motivation: Production rollouts need safer progressive deployment modes (canary, A/B, and shadow) with proactive probing and automatic rollback when composite metrics regress. This PR implements a probing-first staged rollout workflow that combines shadow probing, weighted canary, and A/B branches with an extensible autorollback decision engine.

Summary of changes: adds a probing stage state machine to the rollout controller, a multi-metric autorollback engine that supports composite thresholds and transient-tolerance windows, console wiring to author probing policies, e2e integration tests (simulated traffic + metric regressions), and observability artifacts (dashboards and rollback metrics).

Design highlights: - Probing stage: before shifting traffic to the canary, the controller sends a low-rate shadow/probing stream to the candidate model(s) and evaluates match-rates, latency deltas, and quality eval hooks. Probing results feed the autorollback engine but do not affect production traffic. - Staged probing + canary sequence: once probing passes, we move to a weighted canary (configurable weights/timings). Each progressive step evaluates composite metrics (latency, error-rate, quality score) with hysteresis to avoid flapping. - Autorollback engine: supports composite metric definitions, short/long windows, and a failure budget. It emits structured rollback reasons and integrates with tracing and alerting. - A/B support: rollout can split traffic across two variants and run probes against both; decision engine supports per-variant and cross-variant thresholds.

Files changed (high-level): - rollouts/controller: core state machine and autorollback manager. - docs/ and console/: policy UX and examples. - observability/: dashboard and metrics for rollback reasons and probe health. - tests/: new e2e script that simulates traffic patterns, injected regressions, and validates rollback behavior.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for state transitions and the decision engine, integration e2e script with deterministic fixtures, and dashboard JSON for manual verification. CI: initial runs failed on a flaky timing test (test/rollouts/state_transition_test) -> increased timeouts and added deterministic clocks in tests -> green on latest run.

Review notes and trade-offs: - To avoid blowing up steady-state cost we keep probe sampling low by default and provide explicit policy knobs. - The autorollback engine favors availability (conservative rollouts) with a configurable failure budget so teams can tune tolerance. - We intentionally keep probing logic in the control plane (not on-path) to avoid client-visible latency effects.

Rollback story: when composite thresholds are exceeded, the controller emits a rollback action with structured reason, triggers a canary/AB revert, and records rollback events for the console and long-term audit. There is also a manual-override path for SRE.

Changelog/Release notes: Implement probing-staged shadow -> canary/A-B rollout workflow with multi-metric autorollback. Provides new policy schema, console editor, and observability dashboards.

Related: ENG-4211 (rollout reliability), ENG-4390 (rollback observability), SUP-1024 (customer incident reproducible scenario).
